questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: While balancing a chemical equation, Meera begins by picking out the compound in it that holds the maximum number of atoms, and then works on the element that has the maximum number of atoms inside that compound. Consider the following statements. 1. Meera may have to begin with the compound on the right-hand side, and this happens when the compound holding the maximum number of atoms is a product. 2. The compound holding the maximum number of atoms may be a reactant or a product, and within that compound the element with the maximum number of atoms is the one taken up for balancing first. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

evidence:

that contains the maximum number of atoms. It may be a reactant or a
product.

number of atoms. Using these criteria, we select Fe O and the element

oxygen in it. There are four oxygen atoms on the RHS and only one on
the LHS.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem: Rohit wants the oxygen atoms on the two sides of his unbalanced equation to be equal. He finds 4 oxygen atoms on the right-hand side and only 1 on the left-hand side, and he thinks of correcting this by rewriting the compound on the left so that its formula shows four oxygen atoms. Consider the following statements. 1. Rohit must instead put the coefficient 4 in front of the compound on the left-hand side and leave its formula unchanged, because the formulae of the compounds or elements involved in a reaction cannot be altered. 2. Equalising the number of atoms of an element is possible only when the formulae of the compounds or elements involved in the reaction are altered. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.

evidence:
To equalise the number of atoms, it must be remembered that we
cannot alter the formulae of the compounds or elements involved in the
reactions.

For example, to balance oxygen atoms we can put coefficient
‘4’ as 4 H O and not H O or (H O) .

questions.stem: After putting the coefficient 4 in front of the compound on the left-hand side of his unbalanced equation, Soham counts the hydrogen atoms once more. There are 8 hydrogen atoms on the left-hand side but only 2 on the right-hand side, and he is about to rewrite the right-hand side. Consider the following statements. 1. Soham should write 2 molecules of hydrogen on the right-hand side so that the hydrogen atoms become equal on the two sides. 2. The number of hydrogen atoms on the left-hand side of the partly balanced equation is 2. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are false.
